title: The Empty Cantons — the Quiet Acre
caption: The province sixty leagues south of Sill that the Court names the Empty Cantons and the Fen call the Quiet Acre: roads rutted under turf where no wheel has gone in eight hundred years, six wells dry with their stones laid in the old order, nine doorways standing where the walls have gone with bare squares above three of them and a slate unread in one, cold hearths with white ash unswept, dry cuts dug to drain, and a twelfth doorway left out of the count. Drawn from Gedde's survey of Y.H. 812 and the Greybank annals, with the south road from Sill and Cold Acre, the way in from Greybank, the marsh road to Reedholt and the Standing Post, and the Peat Line and Sere beyond. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 814, the month of Ilmen.
